newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns Serbs against bid to rig Bosnia poll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Serbs against bid to rig Bosnia poll.

text.p: The United States warned Bosnian Serbs on Thursday that they would not be permitted to rig local elections in the disputed town of Brcko.
"We're not going to tolerate any kind of nonsense from the Bosnian Serbs up in Brcko," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
International supervisors in Bosnia said on Thursday they had removed several Serb election officials in an attempt to halt fraudulent registration of voters in Brcko.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said six election officials had been disqualified and that the registration process would be repeated in the Serb-controlled town for municipal polls in September.

"It's very important that the Bosnian Serbs get the message that these elections are not going to be tainted. They're not going to be allowed to be affected negatively by the Bosnian Serbs," Burns told a news briefing.
He said that if the Serbs failed to respect democratic principles they would forfeit Western economic assistance.
"They're not going to be able to succeed in intimidating the OSCE. We will stand up to them. And they will not be allowed to run false elections," Burns said.
Bosnian Serb and Moslem-Croat authorities see the municipal vote in September as a battle for territory contested during the 1992-95 war, particularly in Brcko.
The Serbs, who seized the town at the outset of the war in 1992, are anxious to keep control of Brcko because it serves as the only link between Serb-held territory in western and eastern Bosnia.
The United States and its allies retain key responsibilities for events in Bosnia under terms of the Dayton peace accord, which ended the war between the country's ethnic factions.
